text: General Requirement The degree of Master of Engineering (MEn) is degrees by research work. While formal coursework constitutes a small portion of the programme, the candidate is mainly required to undertake a research project which proves the ability of the candidate in understanding the state-of-art in the candidate's field of studies. In addition, candidates pursuing the MEn degree should demonstrate the potential to pursue an innovative research work. 2. Length of Candidature and Credits The usual length of the candidature is two and half years for MEn During the period of candidature, the candidate is usually supported by a studentship. The formal coursework consists of 52 credits. 3. The main research orientation 1) Modern power electronics converter and control system 2) Modern electric drives motion control system 3) Application of computer and network technology in electric drives system 4) Application of new electronic components in power electronics and electric drives system 4. Confirmation of Study During the first 18 months of candidature, the candidate is compulsorily required to present a seminar reporting on the progress of the project with a written report, which should be no less than 3000 words, with a bibliographic list consisting of no less than 30 books or articles. Upon successful demonstration of satisfactory progress, which has to be endorsed by a review committee, the candidate will be confirmed as being formally admitted to the MEn programme. The review committee includes necessarily no less than 3 professor or associated professors. Assessment The candidate will be examined by the standard of her/his written dissertation, in the form of an MEn Thesis, as well as an oral defence session. The board of Examiners consists of no less than 5 professors, usually more than a half of them are from other universities. The examiners make recommendations to the School Academic Committee who then makes final decision as to the award of the degree to the candidate.
